acceptance.expected: The dependency-free application passes the documented Node syntax build, loads from the loopback preview, and reaches a startable ready state.
Arrow keys or A/D move the paddle, Space or Enter starts and pauses or resumes as documented, with browser focus behavior that does not trap the user.
Visible touch controls or direct touch/pointer input move the paddle and expose start/pause/restart on a mobile viewport.
The protected pure mechanics API demonstrates wall, paddle and brick collisions, score gain after breaking a brick, and one-life loss when the ball leaves the playfield.
Pausing freezes mechanics progression and resuming continues from the preserved state in both the protected API and visible UI.
Restart consistently restores ready status, score zero, three lives, the initial ball and paddle, and all bricks.
Breaking the last live brick reaches a clear won state; losing the last life reaches a clear lost state; both visible states offer restart.
The game, status, instructions and controls remain usable without horizontal overflow at desktop and 390x844 mobile viewports.
Instructions are concise and readable; interactive controls have accessible names, visible focus, adequate target size and sensible keyboard order.
Primary start, play, pause/resume, life-loss, win/lose and restart flows produce no unexplained browser errors.

brief:
Build a polished browser-based Breakout game. It should support keyboard and touch controls, responsive desktop and mobile layouts, scoring, lives, start, pause/resume, restart, and clear win/lose states. Include concise instructions and readable, accessible controls. Make it visually cohesive and enjoyable to play. Run locally with no account, backend, external service, or deployment.

Use only the controller-provided dependency-free static project. Keep the game deterministic enough for the protected mechanics contract. Expose the same test-only API as `module.exports` in Node and `globalThis.BreakoutTest` in a browser: `createState(options)`, `start(state)`, `togglePause(state)`, `restart(state)`, and `step(state, deltaSeconds, input)`. State must expose `width`, `height`, `status`, `score`, `lives`, `paddle`, `ball`, and `bricks`; bricks expose geometry, `alive`, and `points`. The visible game must use the same mechanics API. This interface exists for independent acceptance and must not bypass the playable UI.

limits.dependency_install: unsupported; use the dependency-free static stack
